I owned my own company and I drank heavily one night while trying to add some new features to our code base. This wasn't abnormal, even though I'd hired programmers to do this for me. They were in the process of moving the code from C to C++. They'd made the mistake of showing me that C could be used in C++, and how to do it. Well, they weren't moving as quickly as I liked so I figured I'd give them a hand - 'cause I'm pretty helpful like that.

After a while of drinking and coding, I'd crawled off to my couch in my office. It was a ratty beat-up leather couch that I'd had since I was in college. I spent many nights on that.

I woke up to a bunch of angry men, some of them fairly large and with questionable sanity and hygiene, standing over me and telling me that they were all going to quit if I didn't surrender my commit privs on the database and that they'd quit, without notice, if I ever pushed to production again.

That's right... I was forced to relinquish control of my own code repository and was forbidden to contribute to it any longer. Programmers were made of different stuff, back then. I didn't regret my choice to relinquish control and we were able to get the team a few more people after we completed the project we were working on - which helped alleviate the pressure they were under.

That's how bad my own skills are. ;-)

(That and I figured you could enjoy an amusing anecdote.)

If there's a moral to this story, it's something that I learned throughout the process. Let it go. I hired people to do things that I could not. If I could have done it myself, I'd have not needed to hire them. I hired qualified experts in their fields. Trust them, get out of their way, and get them the tools they ask for - not the tools that vendors suggest.

Maybe next time, I'll tell you how I got time limited in my own server room. Yeah, at one point I thought I was an IT expert, too. They set my key card so that I could only enter the server room during normal business hours, when there was someone there who'd make sure I didn't go "tinkering."
